claims.text: The starting equimolar CoCrFeNiTi is an as-cast, homogeneous simple solid solution without significant short-range order or nanoprecipitates.
A tailored annealing treatment can induce nanoscale short-range order or coherent nanoclusters in equimolar CoCrFeNiTi.
Nanoscale chemically ordered clusters act as local obstacles to dislocation motion.
Formation of short-range order increases localized lattice distortion in CoCrFeNiTi.
The increased lattice distortion associated with short-range order hinders dislocation glide.
The homogeneous as-cast solid solution offers minimal resistance to dislocation motion.
Minimal resistance to dislocation motion causes the relatively low hardness and yield strength of as-cast equimolar CoCrFeNiTi.
Minimal resistance to dislocation motion accounts for the high ductility and machinability of as-cast equimolar CoCrFeNiTi.
Induced short-range order should increase the room-temperature yield strength of CoCrFeNiTi.
Induced short-range order should increase the room-temperature hardness of CoCrFeNiTi.
Induced short-range order should slightly reduce the room-temperature ductility of CoCrFeNiTi.
Thermal activation can assist dislocations in overcoming short-range obstacles.
At 600 °C, thermal activation will weaken the strengthening effect of short-range order in CoCrFeNiTi.
The strength and hardness improvements produced by annealing will be smaller at 600 °C than at 25 °C.
The effect of short-range order on ductility and its stability or uniformity at elevated temperature are uncertain.
TEM and atom-probe tomography can verify the presence and distribution of the induced short-range order.

contradictions.description: Loading is limited to the yield point, but the experiment proposes measuring ductility as percent plastic strain. A meaningful ductility measurement ordinarily requires post-yield deformation, often through failure or a specified plastic-strain endpoint.
